audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-dominant', rule = final syllable (final stress) is correct and now backed by the full text of the best available sources: Carvalho's 2013 MA phonology (sec. 5.2, p.77: stress predictable, always on the last syllable, non-iterative iamb; suffixes and loans shift stress to the new final syllable; compounds primary-final) and his 2017 doctoral grammar (sec. 4.3.1, pp.66-67, with IPA examples [taˈti] ~ [tatiˈni]). The record itself is under-filled: 'quote', 'cite', 'loc', 'grade' are blank and the only text is the abstract sentence. Action: promote the body quotation (2013 thesis p.77 and/or 2017 diss. p.66) into quote/cite/loc, set the strength of the evidence to first-hand descriptive phonology, and add Everett 1995 p.312 (trochaic, L-to-R feet) as a noted older contrary analysis explicitly rejected by Carvalho. no reclassification. sources.citation: de Carvalho, Mateus Cruz Maciel. 2013. Análise fonológica da língua Deni (Arawá). Dissertação (Mestrado em Linguística e Língua Portuguesa), UNESP Araraquara. 108 pp. hdl:11449/93865
sources.quote: 'Na língua Deni, a localização do acento é previsível. Ele cai sempre sobre a última sílaba da palavra, ou seja, a sílaba mais à direita. Sendo assim, padrão acentual é iâmbico não-iterativo' (p.77); suffixed forms and Portuguese loans move stress to the new final syllable; compounds: primary stress on final syllable of second word, secondary on final syllable of first (p.80ff); 'língua com acento fixo, pois o acento principal cai sempre na última sílaba à direita' (p.83).
sources.locator: Resumo (p.9); sec. 5.2-5.2.2, printed pp.77-83 (pp.76-82); Everett 1995 discussed p.39
